gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-old-hun: Noto Sans Old Hungarian reads friendly and current, its big open shapes staying legible even when the text shrinks way down. Starborn can take the larger size.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-old-ita: Dreamy, wide-spaced display letters up top. Noto Sans Old Italic follows with sturdy, tightly proportioned text, and it is happiest at a modest size while Starborn stays free to spread out.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-old-nor: Noto Sans Old North Arabian reads dense and approachable, a tall band of small letters with outward-pointing ends. Starborn is the dreamy opposite, so Noto Sans Old North Arabian would feel crowded if blown up large.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-old-per: Soft starlight spacing above, friendly rounded text below, with Starborn's dark lowercase stripe standing out against it. Starborn is best for drifting, atmospheric lines; Noto Sans Old Permic is best for lines that need to be understood.

Starborn floats, wide-spaced and dreamy, with a dark lowercase stripe. Beneath it Noto Sans Old Persian rises tall and open, letting its clean counters breathe so the page feels light but still grounded.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-old-sog: Dreamy gaps, then crisp text. Starborn spaces its letters out, while Noto Sans Old Sogdian answers with a tall x-height that holds up sharply when shrunk, a contrast that makes each font's job obvious.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Noto Sans Oriya reads friendly and modern, with generous curves. Starborn is best at drifting, dreamy display lines, while Noto Sans Oriya is best at carrying the actual words with small letters nearly as tall as capitals.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-osage: Approachable, first of all, thanks to Noto Sans Osage's inflated lowercase bowls. Starborn's wide-spaced, dark-striped lettering is the dreamy half, and the generous curves of the body keep it from drifting off.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Noto Sans Osmanya reads clean and businesslike, its lowercase looking oversized beside the capitals. And Starborn's wide, starry spacing and dark lowercase stripe give the heading a dreamy lift the sans-serif text happily sits under.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-: Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong brings a high x-height and rounds with little gaps in them. Starborn spreads dreamy, dark-striped letters wide above it, and Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong keeps the lines below compact and grounded.
